title: BSM is a relative-pricing model, not a return forecast
question_investigated: Does Black-Scholes-Merton forecast stock expected returns?
executive_finding: The expected stock drift cancels out of the BSM replication argument. BSM prices options relative to the underlying, risk-free rate, time, and volatility only.
results: Drift term μ disappears from BSM PDE
limitations: None for the theoretical result; empirical fit is imperfect under jumps and stochastic volatility
portfolio_relevance: Do not use BSM to forecast directional returns; use for relative pricing and Greeks only
